CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

What this is

zufft is an R package for fast Fourier, cosine and sine transforms. It is meant to replace fftwtools without FFTW: it bundles the BSD-licensed FFT subset of ducc0, the same files and commit SciPy vendors, so it needs no system library and carries no GPL code. The R API follows scipy.fft conventions (axes, norm, transform types) with names a fftwtools user recognises (fft_c2c(), fft_r2c(), fft_c2r()). It is also a provider: a registered C table lets other packages, first zutsne, call the transforms from C. Zero hard runtime dependencies.

.agents/design.md is the specification and outranks this file. .agents/roadmap.md is the stage plan with exit criteria.

Current state

Verified 2026-10-13: version 0.1.0, ready for CRAN submission. Every stage of the roadmap is merged; cran-comments.md lists the CI legs. What remains is the submission itself, tracked in CRAN-submission (#14). Design questions 9 and 10 are decided: the real transforms halve the first dimension by default, and fused multiply-add contraction is off so results do not depend on workers. Benchmarks against fftwtools are in bench/RESULTS.md.

Stage tracking

Progress toward the next version is tracked as GitHub sub-issues, so the parent issue shows a progress bar such as “6 of 7”.

  • One parent issue per target version, titled with the bare version: v0.1.0 (#2).
  • One sub-issue per roadmap stage, titled as the roadmap titles it, for example Stage 3 — Fourier transforms, and linking to that section.
  • Every tracking issue carries the stage label, so it can be told apart from bug and feature issues and left out of open-issue counts.
  • Close a stage by merging its pull request. Put Closes #<n> in the body of the stage’s pull request. Never close a stage whose exit criteria are not met; record a deviation in the roadmap first.
  • The roadmap stays authoritative. The issues record which stages are done, not what a stage requires. Adding, removing or renaming a stage means editing the roadmap and the sub-issues in the same change.
  • Close the parent issue when CRAN accepts the version and it is tagged. Submission is tracked in CRAN-submission (#14).

Versioning

The package develops at 0.0.0.9000 and targets 0.1.0 for its first CRAN release. Set Version: 0.1.0 and the matching NEWS.md heading when the package enters Pre-flight. Bump to 0.1.0.9000 only after CRAN accepts it.

Until the first release the R API may change freely. The C table in inst/include/zufft.h is different: zutsne will consume it, and a layout change breaks it even before 0.1.0, so the table follows the append-only rules of design §7.

Commands

Run from the package root.

Rscript -e 'devtools::load_all()'                # compile src/ and load
Rscript -e 'devtools::document()'                # roxygen -> NAMESPACE, man/
Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'                    # full testthat suite
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter = "<name>")'   # one test file
Rscript -e 'devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE)'      # order independence
Rscript -e 'devtools::check()'                   # R CMD check
Rscript -e 'devtools::build_readme()'            # README.Rmd -> README.md
air format .                                     # format R sources
tools/vendor/verify                              # vendored tree vs manifest
tools/run-benchmarks --quick                     # design §11 grid, short

tools/run-benchmarks needs zufft installed, plus bench and, for the comparison, fftwtools (system FFTW). The benchmark label on a pull request runs the full grid on a Linux runner.

Testing conventions

  • Self-sufficient. Every test builds its own inputs inside the test_that() block. No file-scope objects.
  • Self-contained. Global state goes through withr::local_*(), randomised input through withr::local_seed(). Tests write only under tempdir().
  • Assert on condition classes, never message text. Use expect_error(..., class = "zufft_invalid_argument") and the other classes of design §9.
  • Order independence. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) is part of the definition of done.
  • Oracles before hand-written cases. scipy.fft fixtures, fftwtools (in Suggests, skipped when absent), stats::fft() and a direct O(n²) DFT (design §10).
  • Keep the suite inside the CRAN time budget of 15 s.

Definition of done

devtools::document() and devtools::check() clean, meaning 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes. The one allowed note is “New submission” before the first release. devtools::test(shuffle = TRUE) green. CI green on every leg. A user-facing change also needs a test, roxygen documentation and a NEWS.md entry.

Releasing to CRAN

  • CI is the pre-submission check. The pedrobtz/r-actions R CMD check runs --as-cran on the CRAN-like runners and containers, and it replaces win-builder, the macOS builder and R-hub. cran-comments.md lists the CI legs as its test environments.
  • The pretest is automated and does not read cran-comments.md. Fix a NOTE instead of justifying it.
  • After acceptance, tag 0.1.0, publish the GitHub release, bump to 0.1.0.9000, and close the version’s parent issue.

Editing rules

  • roxygen comments are the source. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Edit README.Rmd, not the generated README.md.
  • Keep prose simple and short. One idea per sentence. en-GB spelling.
  • Wrap roxygen text at 80 characters and run air format . on R sources.
  • Use lower_snake_case; internal native symbols use the zff_ prefix, the public C API the zufft_ prefix.
  • Keep hard runtime dependencies at zero.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Complex memory is touched only through std::complex in C++. The zero-copy path (design §12.2) is justified on that condition. C glue may pass COMPLEX(x) as a pointer, crop by strides, and copy bytes with memcpy, but must not read or write complex elements as doubles while a shim call can see them. ZFF_COMPLEX_MARSHAL builds the copying fallback; CI keeps it passing.
  • Every shim entry point holds the entry gate (call_gate) around its ducc0 calls. It serialises top-level transforms and grows the pool; ducc0’s plan cache and the fork handlers rely on it.
  • Never unregister or bypass the fork handlers. zff_pool.cpp pins the shared object with RTLD_NODELETE because pthread_atfork handlers outlive an unload (devtools::load_all() reloads).
  • inst/include/zufft.h is a public ABI. Append members only, keep the status values, and keep it compiling standalone as C99 and C++17 (tools/check-header); zutsne will depend on it before 0.1.0.
  • Nothing in the shim or on a pool thread calls R. Errors cross as a status code and a thread-local message; zff_raise() in the C glue turns them into classed R conditions.

Vendored native code

src/ducc0/ is the FFT component of ducc0, exactly the 17 files SciPy vendors in subprojects/duccfft (dual “BSD-3-Clause OR GPL-2.0-or-later”; zufft elects BSD-3). The rest of ducc0 is GPL-only: never copy anything else in.

  • Update only through the tool: tools/vendor/vendor-ducc [SCIPY_COMMIT] takes the ducc0 commit SciPy pins, checks every file against SciPy’s copy and the SPDX line, and rewrites src/ducc0/, tools/vendor/manifest.tsv, tools/vendor/checksums.sha256 and src/zff_version.h. Re-vendor only when SciPy does (design §8).
  • tools/vendor/verify is the offline check CI runs; never edit a file in src/ducc0/. Changes to vendored files go in tools/vendor/patches/, each with its reason; there are two, for clang -pedantic (CRAN’s debian-clang flavor) and for a UBSan finding in the DCT/DST plans. zufft’s adaptations live beside it: the custom threading header, the .cc wrappers and the instantiation units.
  • No -f, -m or -O flag in Makevars. R CMD check warns about them (“checking compilation flags in Makevars”). Fused multiply-add contraction is switched off by src/zff_fp_contract.h, included first in each instantiation unit. tools/check-build-log fails CI on non-portable flags and on any compiled-code NOTE (abort, exit, stdio).
  • Every holder named in the bundled files is in Authors@R and inst/COPYRIGHTS; a re-vendor must re-check that list.

Continuous integration

Workflows come from pedrobtz/r-actions, pinned to @v1: r-cmd-check.yml (quick on pull requests, full on main, full on a pull request with the full-ci label), coverage.yml, vendor.yml and the pkgdown workflow. build-flags.yaml is local: it fails on the NOTEs r-actions lets through. The coverage badge is committed to gh-pages (badges/coverage.svg), because the main ruleset takes no direct pushes; the pkgdown deploy must not force-push or clean that branch.

Commits and pull requests

Short, imperative, sentence-case commit subjects. Keep each commit focused. A pull request explains the user-visible outcome and the rationale, links related issues, lists the checks that were run and the tests that were skipped, and flags platform-sensitive or vendored changes. Performance claims need evidence.
